createDraft.reason: Drives a real browser DOM to write a message: 8-30s+ per call and growing with the content written. A timeout shorter than the write turns one intent into two drafts, because the caller sees a timeout on a write that actually landed.

getThread.reason: Expands EVERY message in the thread before scraping, so cost scales with thread length - and a long many-participant thread is exactly the one whose per-message Cc lines drafting needs for reply-all.

getEmail.reason: A browser read that outlives a 30s kill: killed mid-flight it keeps holding the mailbox's single-flight guard, so the agent's next read is refused busy and it drafts from snippets (2026-09-23).

searchEmails.reason: A browser read that outlives a 30s kill: killed mid-flight it keeps holding the mailbox's single-flight guard, so the agent's next read is refused busy and it drafts from snippets (2026-09-23).

checkEngagedDomains.reason: Runs ONE Gmail search per unknown domain, sequentially, so cost scales with the batch. engaged-domains.ts caps it at MAX_LOOKUPS_PER_PASS and sizes that cap against this timeout: raising the cap without raising this buys nothing.

discardDraft.reason: Operations on one browser session are serialized, so this call's latency includes waiting for whoever else holds the mailbox. Four concurrent callers at ~10s each put the ones at the back past 30s (2026-09-09).

findDraftForThread.reason: Operations on one browser session are serialized, so this call's latency includes waiting for whoever else holds the mailbox. Four concurrent callers at ~10s each put the ones at the back past 30s (2026-09-09).

getDraft.reason: Operations on one browser session are serialized, so this call's latency includes waiting for whoever else holds the mailbox. Four concurrent callers at ~10s each put the ones at the back past 30s (2026-09-09).

getThreads.reason: A BATCH read: opens MANY threads in one held session, so one call legitimately runs minutes. Its result is DATA for its caller, not agent context - ten threads of JSON pass the 100KB context cap and the truncation is silent, which discarded 153s of reads as 'an empty page' (voice crawl, 2026-09-20).
